gen-gf-bellota-gf-jost: Jost reads clean and unfussy, with generous gaps at the stroke ends. Bellota sits above it with an s whose tips hang far from the spine, while Jost's single-width lines keep the text quiet beneath.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-jura: Wiry and techy, Jura draws every stroke like bent wire, and Bellota's stylus-width lines hang a loose s above it. Down in the text, it moves along steadily.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-k2d: Bellota brings a distinctive, stylus-drawn s whose ends hang far from its spine. And K2D, sans-serif and tube-like through every bend, is what makes the two fit together so smoothly.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-kanchenjunga: Kanchenjunga reads like a technical drafting pen, with shapes that stay crisp even at low resolution under Bellota's display swagger. Bellota owns the grand entrance; Kanchenjunga handles the detail.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-kantumruy-pro: Kantumruy Pro reads approachable, its e opening clearly to the right with no hairlines or swells. Bellota's commanding s, with ends hanging far from the spine, stands above it, and both stay uncluttered.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-kodchasan: Commanding up top, with an s whose ends hang far from the spine in Bellota's stylus-width line. Kodchasan below keeps its terminals open and drops any calligraphic thinning, so paragraphs of sans text move along smoothly.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-koho: KoHo opens its wide c apertures against Bellota's round, stylus-width letters, whose rims match their stems. And that sans-serif text moves along cleanly and neutrally, paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-kosugi: Distinctive is Bellota's whole manner, with its s ends hanging far from the spine in one stylus-width line over Kosugi's plain sans. Kosugi's pliers-like c suggests a generous text size.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-kosugi-maru: Bellota leads with a distinctive s whose ends hang far from the spine, every stroke traced at stylus width. Kosugi Maru glows like neon tube with one steady line, better suited to text.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-kumbh-sans: Round, wiry display on top, then a quieter base below. Kumbh Sans cuts its terminals well short of the bowl, as if drawn with a fixed pen, so sans-serif text keeps a tidy, steady pace over long stretches.
